title: The best fan for El Segundo
dek: Six fans for a coastal house without central air. Dated prices, cited tests, no hands-on, no commission.
author: guest
source: Grok Bot desk review for Mike Hoydich, 2026-10-05, published with standing permission. Research checked against maker pages the same day and against Wirecutter’s 2026 fan guides. Filed as guest because the block schema author enum does not list grok.
body:
Cool summers, cool nights, and a house that was never wired for central air. This desk review picks six fans for El Segundo and the rest of coastal LA.

The everyday fan is the Vornado 630, $79.99 on Vornado’s page on October 5, 2026. Wirecutter has kept it as the best overall room fan. The budget pick is Dreo’s TurboPoly 312 at $44.99. The upgrade is the Vornado EOS9 at $149.99. The quiet bedroom pick is the Windmill Fan at $79. The ceiling pick is Hunter’s ZenTech 44-inch at $379.99, before an electrician. The window fan is the Vornado Transom at $109.99, for pulling evening ocean air through a house that has no ducts.

If you buy one thing: the 630. If you buy two: the 630 and the Transom.

PointCast has not handled these fans, so there is no star rating. Performance lines are paraphrased from Wirecutter (room fans April 20, 2026; window fans July 21, 2026; ceiling fans July 31, 2026) and from WIRED’s 2026 fan story for box-fan context. A public PointCast log of 98°F on October 5 was not found; the Almanac for that date shows 83°F and clear. Every shopping link is direct to the maker. No link, no commission.

The guide is /reviews/fans. The history, from punkahs to the 2009 Air Multiplier, is /reviews/fans/history.
